You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`drivers/of/dynamic.c`**:
   - The function signature of `__of_node_dup` was changed to accept a `full_name` string instead of a format string (`fmt`).
   - The implementation of `__of_node_dup` was modified to use `kstrdup` to directly duplicate the provided `full_name`, removing the previous use of `kvasprintf`.

2. **`drivers/of/of_private.h`**:
   - The declaration of `__of_node_dup` was updated to reflect the new parameter type, changing from a format string to a `full_name` string.

3. **`drivers/of/overlay.c`**:
   - The comments were updated to clarify that when creating nodes from a flattened device tree (FDT), the `full_name` will not include the full path.
   - The call to `__of_node_dup` was modified to pass only the basename of the node instead of a full path format string.

4. **`drivers/of/unittest.c`**:
   - The unit tests were updated to call `__of_node_dup` with only the basename of the nodes instead of the full path.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected as follows:

- The change in `dynamic.c` to accept a `full_name` directly is foundational, as it alters how device nodes are created. This change necessitated updates in the header file `of_private.h` to ensure the function signature matches the new implementation.
- The updates in `overlay.c` reflect the new understanding that the `full_name` should only contain the basename, aligning with the changes made in `dynamic.c`. This ensures that the overlay node creation logic is consistent with the new behavior of the device tree.
- Finally, the modifications in `unittest.c` ensure that the unit tests are aligned with the new expectations of the `__of_node_dup` function, validating that the changes made in the other files are correctly implemented and tested. 

Overall, the patch addresses a bug related to the inclusion of full paths in device node names by standardizing the use of basenames across the relevant codebase.

Here is the commit message:
of: overlay: do not include path in full_name of added nodes

Struct device_node full_name no longer includes the full path name
when the devicetree is created from a flattened device tree (FDT).
The overlay node creation code was not modified to reflect this
change.  Fix the node full_name generated by overlay code to contain
only the basename.

Unittests call an overlay internal function to create new nodes.
Fix up these calls to provide basename only instead of the full
path.

Fixes: a7e4cfb0a7ca ("of/fdt: only store the device node basename
in full_name")

Signed-off-by: Frank Rowand <frank.rowand@sony.com>
Signed-off-by: Rob Herring <robh@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the overlay node creation code not being updated to reflect the change in how the `full_name` of device nodes is constructed. Specifically, the `full_name` was expected to contain only the basename of the node, rather than the full path, which was not accounted for in the overlay code. This inconsistency led to incorrect handling of device nodes when created from a flattened device tree (FDT).

Here is the patch:
  * build_changeset_next_level().
  *
- * NOTE: Multiple mods of created nodes not supported.
+ * NOTE_1: A live devicetree created from a flattened device tree (FDT) will
+ *       not contain the full path in node->full_name.  Thus an overlay
+ *       created from an FDT also will not contain the full path in
+ *       node->full_name.  However, a live devicetree created from Open
+ *       Firmware may have the full path in node->full_name.
+ *
+ *       add_changeset_node() follows the FDT convention and does not include
+ *       the full path in node->full_name.  Even though it expects the overlay
+ *       to not contain the full path, it uses kbasename() to remove the
+ *       full path should it exist.  It also uses kbasename() in comparisons
+ *       to nodes in the live devicetree so that it can apply an overlay to
+ *       a live devicetree created from Open Firmware.
+ *
+ * NOTE_2: Multiple mods of created nodes not supported.
  *       If more than one fragment contains a node that does not already exist
  *       in the live tree, then for each fragment of_changeset_attach_node()
  */
 static int add_changeset_node(struct overlay_changeset *ovcs,
 		struct device_node *target_node, struct device_node *node)
 {
 	const char *node_kbasename;
 	struct device_node *tchild;
 	int ret = 0;
 
 	node_kbasename = kbasename(node->full_name);
 
 	for_each_child_of_node(target_node, tchild)
 		if (!of_node_cmp(node_kbasename, kbasename(tchild->full_name)))
 			break;
 
 	if (!tchild) {
-		tchild = __of_node_dup(node, "%pOF/%s",
-				       target_node, node_kbasename);
+		tchild = __of_node_dup(node, node_kbasename);
 		if (!tchild)
 			return -ENOMEM;
 
 		tchild->parent = target_node;
 
 		ret = of_changeset_attach_node(&ovcs->cset, tchild);
 		if (ret)
 			return ret;
 
 		return build_changeset_next_level(ovcs, tchild, node);
 	}
 
 	if (node->phandle && tchild->phandle)
 		ret = -EINVAL;
 	else
 		ret = build_changeset_next_level(ovcs, tchild, node);
 	of_node_put(tchild);
 
 	return ret;
 }
